column1: # These files guard CONFIRMED security defects. JC-011 happened because a
# refactor deleted the regression suites protecting JC-005 and JC-006 and
# reintroduced both defects with nothing failing -- deleting a test never fails
# scripts/qa/check-protected-tests.sh fails CI if a listed file disappears or is
# Removing a line is a DELIBERATE, REVIEWABLE act. Do it only when the defect it
# guards is closed by design (the state is unrepresentable), never to make a
# build green. Migrating a file? Update the path here in the same commit.

column3: JC-005 assist/escalation bypass, JC-006 deactivated-actor internal notes
G-07 phone privacy enforced structurally
BR-1 (PD-7) matrix: NO teacher-parent direct channel, message or call, whatever the relationship, from either side; the PD-6 code is never emitted

BR-1 (PD-7) DB backstop: the database refuses EVERY teacher-parent direct channel, related or not, with the application bypassed (teacher-admin is the positive control); a PD-6-era direct accepts no teacher/parent message and cannot be revived; append-only logs; JC-010

A media token is issued only to a live, authorized participant and carries the smallest grant a voice call needs: roomJoin to one server-named room, no roomCreate, no roomList, no administrative or data capability, a server-resolved identity, a TTL from chat.config alone, and never the API secret; and the CONTROL plane stays separate from the MEDIA plane -- livekit-probe.sh authenticates with server credentials, never calls the participant-token path, only reads RoomService, and keeps its bearer out of argv

A device token can be retired only by its owner, and the call lifecycle drives the seeded incoming_call/missed_call rules: recipients come from the call record and never the payload, the caller is never notified of their own call, repeated reconciliation cannot duplicate a missed_call, and no LiveKit token, room name or contact channel reaches a push payload

An unanswered call always reaches a terminal state: the sweep expires only calls still ringing past the configured chat.config deadline, is idempotent and safe on concurrent workers, never overwrites an answered or ended outcome, leaves answered_at and joined_at null, emits exactly one call.ended/missed, and an expired call can be neither accepted nor granted a media token

Every call lifecycle event is routable and routed to the SERVER-DERIVED CALL PARTICIPANTS, each in their own authenticated actor room: a conversation member who is not a participant (a silent member) receives nothing, a forged payload cannot redirect delivery, one call never reaches another call's participants, a refused action emits nothing, a rolled-back transaction delivers nothing, an outbox retry delivers each participant once, and media-presence events keep conversation-room routing and are never faked from an HTTP accept

Answering a call re-runs the full join authorization (BR-1 per PD-7, contact can_message, on-duty, conversation membership, actor active, left_at, terminal state) and a refusal leaves the record untouched: no joined_at, no answered_at, no status transition, no event, and no false 'answered' outcome in history

The call lifecycle stays internally consistent when application events and real media events race: a decline is terminal as declined and the ring-timeout sweep can never relabel it missed, a terminal call is never resurrected by a late webhook or a second end, an accepted call with no media join is still answered, media leave never ends a call, duration derives from answered_at, and no client names its own call outcome
RT-002/003/004 inverted guards: participant-set authorization, on_behalf_mode attribution
RT-005/007/008 inverted guards: signing secret, attachment validation, SYSTEM-message forgery

RT-024/025 structural backstop, proven against the database with the application bypassed: type immutability, required admin presence, and (PD-7) no direct teacher-parent channel, call or new teacher/parent message (PD-6-era rows readable, lifecycle writes allowed)

Client classification fails closed (PD-6-era rows; under PD-7 a teacherParentDirect is read-only): a direct conversation is only ever teacherParentDirect when the payload states exactly one contact and one teacher by actorKind; absent, ambiguous or role-labelled members classify as unknownDirect and never as an authorized channel

Relationship predicate (PD-6 origin; under PD-7 it opens no channel, asserted in section H): the database's independent answer to which teacher-parent pairs are related, including tenant isolation, liveness, revocation and fail-closed on every unknown
RT-023 fresh-database acceptance: every table, FK, trigger and index a running system needs
RT-001 containment: PR-B closed the HTTP half (no source reads x-actor-id); the WebSocket handshake seam still cannot start outside local/test/ci
PD-2 a parent may join a Student Group call but never start one; BR-1/C-4 still take precedence
RT-001/NF-08 closed: a forged x-actor-id, body or query actorId cannot influence identity; cross-principal, cross-family and cross-organization impersonation refused
RT-001 token forgery: alg confusion, alg=none, unknown kid, foreign issuer/audience, expiry and tampering are each refused
Session revocation is immediate (logout, manager revoke, deactivation) and a replayed refresh token revokes every session on the account

Login rate limiting (IDENTITY-MODEL 4, API-CONTRACT 3.1): password spraying across many accounts is caught by the source budget, which account lockout cannot see; the limiter fails closed and cannot be reset by a success

Authentication audit trail (IDENTITY-MODEL 6): every login, refresh, logout and revocation is recorded in the same transaction as the state change, and refresh-reuse detection cannot revoke sessions without persisting why

Student Group provisioning (API-CONTRACT S-2/S-3, PD-8): parents, teachers and department staff are refused BEFORE the learner lookup and identically for a real or unknown id; only the learner's supervisor, their active backup, their department manager or the super admin; a learner with no supervisor has no group (LEARNER_UNSUPERVISED); another tenant's learner reads as not found; a refusal writes nothing

Student Group provisioning against the real schema (incl. RT-030 Student Group half: a non-default tenant's group and its system messages land in the learner's organization): refusals for parent, teacher, department, inactive, non-supervisor admin and coverage without an active backup link leave conversation/member/message/event/outbox counts unchanged; an unsupervised learner is refused 409 for everyone (PD-8); another tenant's learner is indistinguishable from an unknown one

Conversation membership (API-CONTRACT POST /conversations/:id/members, PD-8): direct conversations are immutable for everyone; only whoever is in charge (supervisor, active backup, department manager, super admin) changes a group; a staff candidate must already be in charge of it; family-group teachers must teach one of its children; tenant isolation; members judged from their own row by kind and role, unknown and cross-tenant ids indistinguishable

Conversation membership against the real schema (PD-8): the Teacher<->Admin direct takeover is refused; out-of-scope, dormant-backup, forged, cross-tenant and malformed requests leave member/audit/outbox counts unchanged; legitimate (supervisor, active backup, department manager), idempotent and concurrent changes and Parent/Teacher messaging still work

RT-030 tenant rules: a direct pair must share one organization (a foreign or SYSTEM actor reads as unknown, before activity is revealed); a write into a conversation requires its organization (a foreign one reads as unknown)

RT-030 on a real database with two organizations: direct conversations, messages and approvals are filed under the trusted organization; cross-organization directs and sends are refused as unknown with no writes, the tenant refusal preceding every attachment check; uniqueness, idempotency, BR-1 (PD-7: a same-tenant teacher-parent direct is refused, no writes) and approval rules hold

RT-009 realtime revocation end to end (real Socket.IO clients, real DB, isolated Redis): every delivery is authorized per recipient at delivery time, so after a removal, logout, refresh reuse or DB-side deactivation completes no node delivers to the revoked socket -- with pushes switched off, with a node dropping every eviction, across both delivery paths, under continuous publication; fails closed when authorization cannot be established; deterministic races prove a removal, logout or DB deactivation cannot return while an already-authorized delivery is pending (row-locked delivery); every locked row type (membership, session, account, staff, teacher, contact) has its own deterministic race; a delivery whose transaction ended emits nothing; a lock wait beyond lock_timeout fails closed and the queue continues; cross-node race through the worker relay; RT-009 completion barrier: a revocation made through the API returns success only after every leased node fenced its in-flight decisions (post-liveness window reproduced with a killed backend and a transaction timeout, one node and two, both delivery paths); an unacknowledging, cut-off or lapsed node never yields a false success, and retries are held to the same barrier; failure model: a frozen node with an expired lease but an open Redis connection, and a lease Redis expires early, are never left out (503); a lost registry is not trusted for a lease

RT-009: the completion barrier fails closed -- with no realtime server attached confirmRevoked refuses (503 COMM.REVOCATION_UNCONFIRMED), and a gateway refusal reaches the caller instead of being swallowed like a push; no REDIS_URL outside APP_ENV=local refuses to boot

RT-031: calls and notifications are filed under their tenant; forged, unknown and stale cross-organization call participants and notification recipients are refused by the database and never delivered to or pushed by the worker; lifecycle updates of historical rows still succeed

RT-032 guarantees: a deactivation written directly to the database (contact, teacher, staff, account) refuses authentication, reads, sends, approvals, call start, media tokens and accept for every operation that starts after it; re-activation restores access

RT-032 closure: every deactivation (UPDATE to not-live or DELETE of a live account/contact/staff/teacher) is journaled in its own transaction by ENABLE ALWAYS triggers, request roles are refused (no GUC opens it), the journal is immutable, RevocationConfirmer stamps confirmed_at only after the completion barrier and retries every failure, the operator procedure never reports success without a confirmation, and send/react/approve/call start/accept/media token re-read liveness under FOR SHARE so none commits after a deactivation; a push scheduled before a deactivation is never sent after it. Mutation-tested (docs/security/DEACTIVATION.md).

RT-037: attachment and story media are served only through the access-checked media route (liveness, account, membership, visibility, deletion, audience and expiry re-checked on EVERY request; the link is bound to attachment/variant/actor); a confirmed deactivation empties every live call room (unconfirmed while the media server refuses); a LiveKit participant_joined by an identity no longer live is undone (503 so LiveKit retries if it cannot be); push payloads carry no content/link/key/token; cross-account operations follow the same revocation; the service_role grant is exactly EXECUTE on chat.invoking_role(). Section G runs against a real LiveKit server when LIVEKIT_REAL_URL is set. Mutation-tested.

RT-037 / W5: over real HTTP, a LiveKit-signed webhook (application/webhook+json, no bearer) reaches the controller -- the global bearer guard and the missing raw-body parser each made every real delivery fail before -- unsigned/tampered ones are refused by the controller's own signature check, and ordinary JSON parsing is unaffected.

RT-037 / RT-039: media links point at MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, else the origin the request reached the API at (X-Forwarded-Host only behind a declared trusted proxy), never a developer localhost default; a hostile Host builds no link.

Approval decisions: approve/reject and double-approve races leave exactly one decision whose stored state matches what was announced; a cross-organization manager and an out-of-scope admin cannot decide; concurrent sends get gap-free distinct seqs

PD-7 side channels: a PD-6-era direct teacher-parent conversation stays readable but refuses new reactions, messages, attachment uploads and calls from either side; the Student Group still allows them

Staff scope (PD-8): staff read only on a resolved basis -- neither a membership row nor the manager role admits on its own; the super admin takes part; another organization reads as not found; the fact defaults to false; canSend resolves the basis itself and derives the attribution from it (owner / coverage / assist / escalation, JC-005 refusals)
A database or Redis failure during a socket handshake costs that socket (transport close), never the API process; a refused token is still a server disconnect
Outbox claim precision (issue #29), deterministic: a row stamped 1 ms after the drain clock is claimed by that drain; retry backoff still honoured; a row is never claimed twice

PD-8 end to end on a seeded synthetic organization: every staff member x every conversation (list and per-conversation read) against an oracle from the seed plan; another supervisor, teacher or parent gets nothing by id over HTTP, socket or attachment path; foreign and unknown ids answered identically (404); backup activation/expiry, reassignment and family-group creation over HTTP incl. who may NOT; RLS on chat.message as chat_app

PD-8 revocation: a child moved away, a backup deactivated/expired/ended or leaving the department, a manager replaced -- each ends access at once on list, page, detail, note and approval queue; family ownership, on_duty() and sticky grant nothing

D1 (PD-A) on the PD-8 line: a department manager, an ACTIVE backup or the super admin who may send in a conversation they are not a member of cannot START a call there (no phantom call; nothing written; capability agrees); D3: every call operation answers another organization exactly like an unknown id (404)
